title: Derived Hom computed by a bounded-above projective resolution
statement: Let $A$ be a ring, let $F$ and $G$ be $A$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $E^\bullet\to F[0]$ be a quasi-isomorphism from a bounded-above complex of projective $A$-modules. Then the cochain complex $\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(E^\bullet,G[0])$ represents $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(F[0],G[0])$, and hence its $i$-th cohomology is canonically $H^i(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(F[0],G[0]))$ for every $i\in\mathbf Z$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom].

source.place: derived Hom computed from projective resolutions (the projective-resolution construction of RHom); compare More on Algebra Tag 0A64 and Derived Categories Tag 06XR

proof.text: View the bounded-above complex $E^\bullet$ as a complex in the homotopy category of $A$-modules. The Mathlib K-projectivity statement [lem-sc-bounded-above-projective-kprojective] applies to the abelian category of $A$-modules, so applying $\operatorname{Hom}_A(E^\bullet,-)$ to an acyclic complex preserves acyclicity. The quasi-isomorphism $E^\bullet\to F[0]$ therefore computes the total derived Hom by the ordinary Hom complex in the definition [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], so $\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(E^\bullet,G[0])$ is a representative of $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(F[0],G[0])$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 06XR (derived-lemma-compute-ext-resolutions), projective-resolution construction of derived Hom

proof.text: The Hom complex is formed degreewise by the products $\prod_j\operatorname{Hom}_A(E^j,G[0]^{j+i})$, with differential induced by the differentials of $E^\bullet$ and $G[0]$. This is exactly the product totalization specified by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]; because $G[0]^q=0$ for $q\ne0$, its degree-$i$ term reduces to $\operatorname{Hom}_A(E^{-i},G)$, with the induced differential. The comparison is canonical because the derived-Hom functor sends the quasi-isomorphism $E^\bullet\to F[0]$ to an isomorphism after K-projective replacement.

source.place: Lemma Tag 06XR, construction of the Hom complex from a projective resolution

proof.text: Applying the cohomology functor in degree $i$ to the representative from Step 1 gives $H^i(\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(E^\bullet,G[0]))\cong H^i(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(F[0],G[0]))$. The isomorphism is canonical because [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] is a functor on the derived category and the K-projective comparison is unique in that category; it is therefore independent of the chosen resolution and natural in $F$ and $G$. It holds for every integer $i$, including negative degrees (where both sides vanish in the module-in-degree-zero situation when appropriate).
